setting: work teams in a large multi-site manufacturing and services firm
research_question: What determines team performance in this firm, and in particular how does team turnover affect team performance, through which mechanisms, and under what conditions?

variables.name: team_turnover
variables.label: Share of team members who left and were replaced during the year (standardized index)

variables.name: team_performance
variables.label: Supervisor-rated team performance against annual targets (standardized index)

variables.name: knowledge_loss
variables.label: Loss of team-specific procedural knowledge, from quarterly skills audits (standardized index)

variables.name: idea_novelty
variables.label: Novelty of the team's submissions to the firm's improvement program, rated by independent judges (standardized index)

variables.name: routine_codification
variables.label: Degree to which the team's work procedures are documented in written routines (standardized index)

variables.name: task_interdependence
variables.label: Degree to which members' tasks depend on one another's outputs (standardized index)

variables.name: hiring_quality
variables.label: Quality of replacement hires, from structured assessment scores at entry (standardized index)

variables.name: workload
variables.label: Average weekly workload per member relative to the firm norm (standardized index)

variables.name: budget_slack
variables.label: Unspent discretionary budget available to the team (standardized index)

variables.name: training_investment
variables.label: Hours of formal training purchased for the team (standardized index)

literature.design: Panel of 212 manufacturing teams over four years.
literature.mechanism: The authors attribute the pattern to the loss of tacit, team-specific knowledge.

literature.design: Field study of 96 software teams with quarterly skills audits.
Survey of 340 service teams in two retail chains.
literature.mechanism: Documented routines are argued to buffer teams against the disruption of member exit.

literature.design: Cross-sectional study of 1,105 teams in a logistics firm.
literature.mechanism: The authors recommend expanding formal training budgets.

literature.design: Archival study of 2,300 hires in a professional services firm.
